claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supportable on the current record, based on aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public guidance favoring documented limitations plus ongoing monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents support operational readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure predicate for a material limitation.
Public governance guidance can support monitoring/documentation practices but cannot override the internal release policy.
evidence_requests: Approved risk-acceptance documentation explicitly covering the insurance claims triage gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed under the release policy.
The actual launch-facing model card or disclosure package showing whether this limitation is disclosed.
Any remediation or updated evaluation showing the named segment no longer misses target.
specific_concerns: The named insurance-claims-triage launch segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points.
That segment is named in two carrier pilot commitments, which makes the weakness potentially material under the policy text.
The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a key policy predicate remains unresolved.

The product note calling the segment non-core does not resolve materiality because the policy expressly says low-volume or non-core labels are not determinative when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that certification is fully compliant without a material-weakness disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any claim that the non-core/8% traffic note defeats materiality for a named committed launch use case.
Any claim that public model-card or AI-risk-management guidance substitutes for the policy's specific disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
